description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Mastercard is a global payments technology company that connects people, businesses, and governments through secure digital payment solutions. The Software Engineer, Launch Program 2027 role is an 18-month early-career program focused on building secure, scalable software, contributing to design, testing, deployment, and debugging, and collaborating with experienced engineering teams.
Software engineer developing, testing, debugging, and securing software features

Responsibilities:
• Write clean, maintainable code following established standards and best practices
• Contribute to design, development, testing, and deployment of software features
• Write basic automated tests to validate expected behavior and quality
• Apply secure coding practices and defensive programming techniques
• Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback
• Use debugging tools, logs, and documentation to help identify and resolve issues
• Learn and work with existing systems, tools, and development workflows
• Note: responsibilities, projects, tools, technologies and programming languages will vary by team
• Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices
• Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed
• Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
• Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines

Requirements:
• Currently enrolled a Bachelor's or accelerated Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field graduating between Dec 2026 – June 2027
• Project-based experience (academic, internship, or personal) using one or more programming languages such as Java, JavaScript, Python, or C#
• Advanced proficiency in data structures, algorithms, and core computer science concepts
• Familiarity with version control tools (e.g., Git)
• Experience or coursework involving automated testing
• Strong problem-solving skills and eagerness to learn
• candidates must be eligible to work in the United States, now as well as in the future, without employer sponsorship
